items.title: Warhammer Survivors Lands Nov. 10 on 7 Platforms [2026]
items.summary: Warhammer Survivors launches Nov. 10, 2026 on PS5, Xbox, Switch 2, Switch, PC and mobile at $7.99, with Game Pass day one.
items.content:
Warhammer Survivors now has a release date, and it lands on nearly every screen a player owns. Developer and publisher Auroch Digital confirmed on October 6, 2026 that the bullet-heaven roguelike launches on November 10, 2026 across PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2, Nintendo Switch, PC, iOS, and Android, according to the official Auroch Digital game page . The simultaneous seven-platform rollout is unusual for a Games Workshop license, and it puts a $7.99 Warhammer title directly in the path of millions of Xbox Game Pass subscribers on day one.

Warhammer Survivors Release Date: November 10 Across Seven Platforms What Is Warhammer Survivors? Auroch Digital’s Take on the Survivors Genre Confirmed Platforms, Storefronts and Pricing Xbox Game Pass Day-One Availability: What It Actually Means Playable Champions: Morvenn Vahl, Lyssa Revenya and a 40-Plus Roster Why Character Count Matters for Replay Value The Steam Demo: What You Can Already Play Vampire Survivors and the Bullet-Heaven Boom: Historical Context Warhammer Licensing in Games: A Crowded 2026 Battlefield Market Impact: Why a Sub-$8 Game Is Worth Tracking Competitive Comparison: Warhammer Survivors vs the Survivors-Like Field Switch 2 and Switch Support: Reaching Nintendo’s Full Install Base What’s Still Unconfirmed Ahead of Launch Predictions: What Happens After November 10 How Warhammer Survivors Fits the Bigger Budget-Game Trend Frequently Asked Questions When does Warhammer Survivors release? What platforms is Warhammer Survivors available on? How much does Warhammer Survivors cost? Is Warhammer Survivors on Xbox Game Pass? Can I play Warhammer Survivors before launch? Who is developing Warhammer Survivors? Which characters are confirmed playable? Is Warhammer Survivors similar to Vampire Survivors? Related Coverage The announcement caps nearly a year of buildup since Auroch Digital first teased the project in November 2025. What started as a niche crossover between Games Workshop’s grimdark universes and the Vampire Survivors-style genre has turned into one of the most-searched gaming stories of the week, with “warhammer survivors” pulling roughly 4,400 monthly searches in the US, per DataForSEO keyword data pulled October 7, 2026. Here is what is confirmed, what is still murky, and why a budget-priced spinoff matters more than its price tag suggests.

Auroch Digital’s own storefront page lists the launch date plainly: Warhammer Survivors “will launch on November 10th on PC (Steam and GOG), Nintendo Switch 1 and 2, PlayStation 5, Xbox series X|S and mobile (iOS and Android),” according to the developer’s official page . That is seven distinct platforms shipping on the same day, a logistical bet that few mid-budget licensed games attempt. Sony confirmed its side of the release independently. The PlayStation Blog posted on October 6, 2026 that the studio is “excited to announce that Warhammer Survivors launches on PS5 November 10,” pairing the date with new character reveals.

What the headline coverage has mostly skipped is that mobile is part of the day-one plan too. Reports confirm iOS and Android versions ship alongside the console and PC builds, meaning Warhammer Survivors is not just a desktop curiosity. It is a cross-platform launch built to catch players wherever they already spend time with Games Workshop properties, from tabletop hobby shops to phone screens on a commute.

Auroch Digital first revealed the project in a November 2025 blog post, describing it as “a frenetic roguelike Survivors game based in the Warhammer universes,” according to the studio’s original reveal . The phrase “Survivors game” is a deliberate nod to the genre popularized by Vampire Survivors, where a single character auto-attacks waves of enemies while the player chooses upgrades and dodges incoming swarms. Warhammer Survivors takes that loop and reskins it with Games Workshop factions, pulling from both the Warhammer Fantasy and Warhammer 40,000 settings based on the confirmed character roster.

That genre choice is strategic. Survivors-likes are cheap to build relative to a full tactics or shooter title, run on nearly any hardware, and have proven they can sell in the millions on a small budget. Pairing that low-friction format with one of gaming’s most recognizable licenses lets Auroch Digital chase a broad audience without the production costs of a full 40K squad shooter or RTS.

The pricing is consistent across regions and has been locked for weeks ahead of launch. On Steam Community, Auroch Digital wrote that the studio is “pleased to finally announce that Warhammer Survivors launches on 10th November 2026 for the price of £6.39 | $7.99 | €7.49,” confirming the figure directly via the official Steam Community page . A 10% launch and pre-order discount is also live on select storefronts, which would put the US price closer to $7.19 for anyone who commits before the window closes.

Seven platforms at one flat price point is a rare structure in 2026’s gaming market, where premium remasters routinely launch past $70 (see how the Kingdom Hearts III + Re Mind Switch 2 port was priced at launch) and even mid-tier licensed games often carry $20-30 entry costs. Warhammer Survivors is positioned closer to an impulse buy than a flagship release, which matters for how it will be judged commercially.

The Xbox Game Pass inclusion is the detail driving a chunk of the search interest around this launch. IGN’s coverage of the release date reveal states plainly that “If you have Xbox Game Pass, you’ll be able to play it at no extra charge on day one,” according to the outlet’s release coverage . What is not yet nailed down publicly is which specific Game Pass tier unlocks it, since Microsoft has run multiple membership levels in 2026 after reshuffling pricing earlier in the year. The announcement itself just says “Game Pass,” without the tier breakdown that would tell subscribers on cheaper plans whether they are covered.

That ambiguity is worth tracking given how much scrutiny Game Pass has faced over value perception in 2026. Subscriber churn and price hikes have been recurring storylines, documented in reporting on Game Pass subscriber losses following a 50% price increase . Adding a cheap, high-replayability roguelike to the day-one lineup is a low-cost way for Microsoft to pad out that value argument, regardless of which tier eventually gets confirmed.

Character reveals have been the steady drip-feed keeping the game in gaming headlines since the original announcement. Two confirmed playable characters stand out by name: Morvenn Vahl, the Warhammer 40,000 Adepta Sororitas commander, and Lyssa Revenya, a figure from the Warhammer Fantasy side of the setting. Pulling leads from both settings in the same roster is a signal that Auroch Digital is not picking a single Warhammer universe to favor, but blending them into one survivors-style cast.

The studio has also confirmed the roster runs past 40 playable champions at launch, a notably large cast for a budget-priced survivors title. Vampire Survivors itself didn’t reach a comparable character count until well after multiple content updates and paid DLC packs. Shipping that volume of characters on day one suggests Auroch Digital is leaning on the breadth of the Warhammer IP, where decades of miniatures, codexes and army books already exist as a built-in character bible, rather than designing an original cast from scratch.

In the survivors genre, character variety is the primary replay hook once a player clears the early difficulty curve. Each character typically changes starting weapons, passive bonuses and synergy options, turning a single map into dozens of viable runs. A 40-plus roster at launch, if it holds up once players get hands-on time, gives Warhammer Survivors a deeper starting library than most competitors ship with even after a year of updates.

Unlike most licensed games that stay locked behind marketing embargoes until launch week, Warhammer Survivors already has a playable PC demo live on Steam. IGN’s reporting ties the release-date reveal directly to “a new demo you can play right now,” per the outlet’s headline . The demo gives players more than a month of hands-on time before the full release, functionally extending the marketing window and letting word-of-mouth build ahead of November 10.

At Polygon, he covers gaming and entertainment news, reviews new video games, interviews behind-the-scenes talent, and more. He enjoys discovering hidden gems and sharing them with Polygon's audience. Previously, he was the gaming editor for AIPT Comics and has written for other outlets like XDA, How-To Geek, and The List. He enjoys soulslikes, character-driven RPGs, and third-person shooters plucked straight out of the Xbox 360 era. He also likes to flex his non-video game nerdy knowledge sometimes, whether that's explaining who's who in the new Wolverine game or recommending a comic book series about a sentient sword. Games like Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered and Barbie Rewind are dropping in November. And now, Warhammer is about to join them.

On Tuesday, developer and publisher Auroch Digital announced that Warhammer Survivors will be released Nov. 10, right in between Zelda and GTA. It's a roguelike bullet heaven, also called a "survivorslike," popularized by Vampire Survivors . Poncle, developer of Vampire Survivors , has partnered with Warhammer to bring its expertise to Warhammer Survivors .

Image: Auroch Digital The frantic bullet heaven gameplay of Vampire Survivors heads to Warhammer 40,000's grimdark 41st Millennium and Age of Sigmar's the Mortal Realms setting. Unlock over 40 characters from the Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer Age of Sigmar universes, each of whom will play differently with unique weapons and stats. Face down endless hordes of monstrous enemies, and go toe-to-toe with tough Extremis Bosses, which will be difficult even for Vampire Survivors veterans.

Warhammer Survivors will retail for $7.99. It will be released Nov. 10 on Android, iOS, Nintendo Switch, Switch 2, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X. It won't be the only Warhammer 40,000 game fans will get this year. Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 , a real-time strategy game, will be out in December after a recent delay.

items.title: 2026's Best Game Comes To Mobile Next Week
items.summary: 2026's best game so far is finally coming to more platforms, letting mobile audiences become as hopelessly addicted as console and PC players.
items.content:
Image Via Poncle By Scott Baird Published Oct 6, 2026, 10:28 AM EDT Scott Baird is a Contributor at DualShockers with over a decade of experience writing about video games, board games, and tabletop RPGs. He has been writing professionally since 2013 and covering games since 2018, with work spanning news, reviews, lists, guides, interviews, and event coverage. Before joining DualShockers, Scott contributed to publications including The Escapist , Dexerto , TheGamer , CBR , and Gamepur . He has also worked as a full-time Pokémon writer at Dexerto and a features writer at TheGamer. Scott holds a Bachelor’s Degree in Film & TV Production . Sign in to your DualShockers account Add Us Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap The best game of 2026 so far is coming to more platforms, as its developer has announced that it will be arriving on Android and iOS devices next week, in addition to its Steam and console ports.

All anyone can talk about when it comes to GOTY 2026 is Grand Theft Auto 6 , to the point where it's practically considered a given in every award category. There are a lot of assumptions that the game will be some all-time classic, based on the development time and money put into it, but nothing is guaranteed, as fans might be left disappointed by it not meeting their expectations.

To unlock the Pentagram in Vampire Crawlers, the player needs to go on an incredibly dangerous mission.

Balatro proved that indie puzzle games can be the biggest titles of the year, and for 2026, Vampire Crawlers could be the shock award winner. Even more people will be playing it soon, as the official Vampire Crawler Steam page has revealed when the game is coming to mobile devices, which will be the ideal way to experience its dungeon exploration and card combos.

Close Image Via Poncle Image Via Poncle Image Via Poncle Image Via Poncle window.arrayOfGalleries["article-gallery-1-245616961"] = '" Close Image Via Poncle Image Via Poncle Image Via Poncle Image Via Poncle "'; According to developer Nosebleed Interactive, Vampire Crawlers is coming to Android and iOS on October 12, 2026. Unlike Vampire Survivors, which requires careful and accurate movement to escape from crowds of enemies, Vampire Crawlers is a turn-based game that can be played at a leisurely pace, making it an ideal mobile title.

The news post also confirmed the addition of the Karoma's Mana item, which switches cards out, depending on its cost. Karoma's Mana also features the Adaptability keyword, which changes a card's cost to one more than the last one played, meaning it can always continue a combo. Adaptability can be added to any card via its new gem , assuming players find it in a dungeon.

Even more people will be playing it soon, as the official Vampire Crawler Steam page has revealed when the game is coming to mobile devices, which will be the ideal way to experience its dungeon exploration and card combos.

A new Arcana is also being added to Vampire Crawlers. This Arcana is called Chair Game, and it activates when the player cannot continue a chain. Chair Game can switch up to four cards, discarding old ones in the process, and potentially activating Afterlife effects. Using Chair Game will be especially helpful in Vampire Crawlers' endless mode , where powerful combos are necessary for survival.

Vampire Crawlers is one of, if not the best games of 2026, which is no small boast, considering how many incredible titles have launched this year, and are still to come. There's still The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and Grand Theft Auto 6 launching in November, meaning the attention of the gaming world will be drawn to them, leaving many worthy games in the dust.

Hopefully, the awards season won't be monopolized by a handful of games, even though that's exactly what's being predicted. Vampire Crawlers is an incredibly addictive game, whose main drawback was a lack of content at launch, as it was easy to 100% the game in a desperate frenzy, while getting a hit of that combo goodness. The developers have been adding new content since launch, so even the main issue is being diluted over time.

Poncle continues to grow the Vampire Survivors universe, with upcoming crossovers with Warhammer and Jujutsu Kaisen. Vampire Crawlers deserves a similar treatment, and will hopefully get its own crossover events in the future to keep it in the public eye. With the mobile ports on the way, countless more people have the chance to jump into the dungeon and start crawling.

The studio behind Vampire Crawlers has revealed how the game came about, thanks to its relationship with the creator of Vampire Survivors.

items.title: Warhammer Survivors Launches November 10 for Switch 2, PS5, Xbox Series, Switch, PC, and Game Pass
items.summary: Developer Auroch Digital announced the Survivors-like game, Warhammer Survivors, will launch for the Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, [...]
items.content:
Developer Auroch Digital announced the Survivors-like game, Warhammer Survivors , will launch for the Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, Nintendo Switch, PC via Steam and Microsoft Store , Xbox Game Pass, iOS, and Android on November 10 for $7.99 / £6.39 / €7.49.

Warhammer Survivors is a fast-paced roguelite survivors’ game, pitting a host of iconic Warhammer characters against endless hordes of enemies from multiple Warhammer factions.

Developed by Auroch Digital ( Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun ) in partnership with Warhammer and poncle ( Vampire Survivors ), discover the universes of Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer: Age of Sigmar in all its pixel glory in this new surviv-a-ton.

Choose your universe and engage in frenetic battles across the open and ashen plains of Aqshy to the tight and confined corridors of an abandoned Space Hulk. Every stage is a new arena of slaughter, each with its unique enemy faction… and secrets to uncover.

Select from a roster of renowned champions from both the Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer Age of Sigmar universes. Play as the mighty Space Marine Sternguard Veteran, Malum Caedo, and the lightning-forged Stormcast, Neave Blacktalon, among a host of others. Each character comes with unique weapons and starting stats—no two survivors play the same.

Here are just some of the playable characters and the enemy factions they will face:

Wield an arsenal of iconic weapons drawn from the armories of the far future and the Mortal Realms. Eviscerate Tyranid hordes with a chainsword, or pulverize enemies with the unrelenting Bolter… and, if all that doesn’t work, drown them in a pot of Citadel Nuln Oil paint.

Mix and match weapons with power-ups and evolve them into devastating new forms to create screen-clearing storms of bullets, blades, and magic.

Obliterate the skittering, beady-eyed Skaven and their horde of warp-addled abominations or stand your ground against the ravenous Tyranid swarm and its myriads of monstrous Xenos Bioforms. Bring your weapons to bear against the endless hordes of these factions (and more) from the Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer Age of Sigmar universes!

Death is not the end for these champions of endless war. A growing roster of unlockable characters, weapons, abilities, and rare relics will increase your odds of survival.

items.title: Warhammer Survivors is more than just a Vampire Survivors spin-off
items.summary: Even as we drown in Warhammer games, Survivors stands out as something extremely cool.
items.content:
Even as we drown in Warhammer games, Survivors stands out as something extremely cool.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Auroch Digital) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter I thought Warhammer Survivors sounded like a neat spin-off—Vampire Survivors in a Warhammer skin, created by Boltgun developer Auroch Digital. Having spent 10 hours with its demo, however, I'm increasingly convinced that it deserves to be catagorised as a sequel.

A lot of care has clearly gone into the hero design, maps and all the horrible beasties trying to eviscerate you, and rather than simply replicate Vampire Survivors, Auroch Digital has included a bunch of novelties and new ideas, like followers and more overt boss battles.

Playing it on my Steam Deck has already had a terrible impact on my sleep routine, just like its predecessor. And with its launch just around the corner on November 10, I think I'm just going to have to accept that I'm going to be very tired for the rest of the year.

Weapon evolutions, enemies that drop chests with multiple items, arcana, bosses, challenges, upgrades—if it's in Vampire Survivors, it's probably in Warhammer Survivors, albeit with some Warhammer-themed twists. Instead of experience gems, for instance, you get experience skulls (because of course you do). And instead of Red Death, you get Extremis bosses, massive seemingly invincible bastards—until you figure out the trick to destroying them.

I have used buckets of Nuln oil in my Warhammer painting endeavours—and yes, I've spilled a lot of it. On my jeans, on my carpet, one time on my dog. But it's never hurt anyone. In Warhammer Survivors, it's been weaponised, damaging and slowing ememies, as well as making them more flammable. You'll also be able to get your hands on explosive dice, which roll across the battlefield before going kaboom! I'm sure there are rules against this.

The first WH40k map sees you running around a battlefield that's being swallowed up by tyranids. It's aggressively pink and full of horrible pustules and grotesque alien topography. In Age of Sigmar, meanwhile, it's skaven time! Nasty little rodents, glowing warpstones, you know the deal. There's even a map that's just your tabletop, full of paints and measuring tape, where all the game's monstrosities gather together to take you out.

While Warhammer Survivors is a singleplayer romp, that doesn't mean you're all alone. Unlockable characters can be rescued once you defeat the enemies harassing them, after which they'll join you in battle. In subsequent fights, they'll rejoin you when you select one of their associated weapons when you level up. At least one character gets buffs from having more followers, and upgrading his lasgun also lets him run around with his fellow Astra Militarum grunts.

I've poured hundreds of hours into Vampire Survivors, and Warhammer Survivors might be a bit trickier. Battles escalate a lot faster, and it took me longer to figure out good weapon combos that worked to thin the herd. I was a lot more desperate for healing than I'm used to with its predecessor. I think I'd prefer the early game to be slightly less intense, though the issue might be that the demo features fewer weapons and characters, which could be making it feel a touch more challenging than it actually is.

Enemy factions benefit from unique traits that may give you a bit of a hard time. Tyranids, for instance, can be empowered by more intelligent members of their species, which use their synapse power to enrage lesser critters within their radius. So you'll want to take these psychic beasties down quickly. Orks, meanwhile, can get all riled up, kicking off a WAAAGH, where they spawn in greater numbers and become faster and stronger.

When you play Warhammer Survivors, you select a universe first. Characters, upgrades and unlocks are specific to each universe, though you will find some passive abilities repeated in both. It feels like two spin-offs collected in a single game.

Vampire Survivors is the game that really justified my purchase of a Steam Deck, and while developer Auroch Digital still says it's working on compatibility, it already feels great on my Deck. It's where I've spent most of my time playing it and I've got no complaints.

Cancel all of your plans in November, because Warhammer Survivors is launching on the 10th. And I've got high hopes for it. Yes, it's a spin-off, but it also feels like a proper Vampire Survivors sequel and potentially my favourite bullet heaven since the OG.

items.title: Warhammer's Vampire Survivors-Like Brings Insane Pixel Action to PS5 in November
items.content:
Warhammer Survivors , the Warhammer game that's quite clearly taken inspiration from Vampire Survivors , now has a confirmed release date on PS5.

Unfazed by the looming shadow of GTA 6 , the chaotic roguelite title launches on the 10th November, priced at £6.39 / $7.99 / €7.49.

There'll also be a 10% discount on release, and if you pre-order, but only on "select" platforms. We don't yet know if that includes Sony's current-gen console.

It sounds like Bristol-based developer Auroch Digital's stuffed as much content into Warhammer Survivors as it can. The game features over 40 playable characters from throughout Warhammer 40,000 and Age of Sigmar lore, and you can wield over 75 types of weapons.

Are you up for crushing waves upon waves upon waves of humanity's enemies? Never stop blasting in the comments section below.

items.title: Warhammer Survivors Is Shaping Up to Be a Clever and Deep Adventure Featuring Warhammer 40,000 and Age of Sigmar
items.summary: Warhammer Survivors is shaping up to be another great adventure for fans of both Vampire Survivors and Warhammer, and I’m excited to see how the full game unfolds and adds to the fun I experienced in this short demo. It’s not doing anything groundbreaking, from what I can tell, but it has added meaningful additions that really honor the source material in a unique way that benefits gameplay. All I know is that all I want to do is jump back in for one… more… round… and that’s one of the highest compliments you can give any game.
items.content:
There are few things more rewarding than the tide turning in your favor in Vampire Survivors. Starting as a weak soldier with one small attack and a fear of even the smallest foe, you soon become a literal weapon of mass destruction and turn a bullet hell of enemies into your own personal bullet heaven.

And you know what can make that feeling even better? Doing it with some trusty allies from the Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer Age of Sigmar universes while using weapons pulled not just from the lore, but those inspired by how we engage with the tabletop game. Yes, we’re talking about the very dice we roll and paint we use to bring our miniatures to life. That, my friends, is Warhammer Survivors.

Warhammer Survivors is a standalone game developed and published by Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun’s Auroch Digital in partnership with Vampire Survivors’ Poncle, and it initially feels like returning home to the original title. However, you’ll quickly start to notice that it does enough things to stand tall on its own.

I spent a few hours with the demo you can download right now on PC via Steam and Xbox ahead of its November 10, 2026 release date, and I was able to check out both the Warhammer 40,000 side of the game and the Warhammer Age of Sigmar side. You read that right, there are two separate games included with their own unlocks, stages, achievements, and more.

We’ll start in Warhammer 40,000, as I first jumped into the armored shoes of Boltgun’s Malum Caedo, who starts with the Chainsword that is the weapon of choice for those within the Imperium of Man. However, in Vampire Survivors fashion, you quickly level up and gain access to new Weapons and Passives that make you increasingly more powerful.

As I teased before, you’ll find Boltguns and Lasguns and even Whirlwind Batteries that rain down missiles from above, but it’s the tabletop-inspired items that got me the most excited. If you are entrenched in the Warhammer universe, you’ll be very familiar with Nuln Oil, a very popular shade of paint. In Warhammer Survivors, this becomes a weapon that targets groups of enemies and damages them by splashing them with flammable oil.

Another fun weapon is the D6 Dice, which is inspired by the same dice that fuel its tabletop games. In Warhammer Survivors, these are represented by massive dice that come flying in off screen and will explode depending on what number they land on.

So not only are these giving a nod to the tabletop experience in a clever way, but they are giving it some serious gameplay ramifications, as enemies drenched in this Nuln Oil are even more susceptible to fire damage. This is all taken to greater heights when you learn there is an actual Hobby Table stage that has you playing on a workstation and that there’s a Paint Pot system that unlocks characters when certain combinations of colors are used. These little touches are so clever and don’t feel forced, they feel earned and welcome and add to the entire experience, just like the ally system.

In traditional Vampire Survivors, players are facing an endless horde of enemies by themselves and an array of weapons that fly in every direction away from and around them. In Warhammer Survivors, you get to bring some NPC friends along for the ride, and it’s awesome.

If you played Vampire Survivors’ Ode to Castlevania DLC, you’ll have a base understanding of how this works as they had a similar Familiars system, but you’ll be able to recruit other characters from the Warhammer universe to help you out on your run by choosing to select the weapons they would normally wield in the canon.

As an example, I may have started as Malum Caedo, but I was able to quickly add Trooper Bartosz Kozlowski to my crew (after I rescued him on the map from a circle of enemies and unlocked him as a playable character!) by choosing the Lasgun weapon. He followed me around and shot las bolts at the nearest enemy, and even more Astra Militarum troops joined as I leveled up the weapon. It honestly gave me the slightest link to Mass Effect 2, as I looked forward to recruiting all my allies for this epic war each run presented me with.

As for the runs themselves, they lasted anywhere from five minutes to over 20, and I enjoyed how there were always things to chase after. One of these objectives, which is represented by a question mark, is how you find characters like Trooper Bartosz Kozlowski or The Legend of Catachan. The latter character was the biggest challenge of the demo for me as he was surrounded by a circle of Warriors, who all used their Synapse Emitters to make any enemies within a close range of them even more powerful. Conquering that and unlocking The Legend of Catachan with a fun Super Smash Bros.-esque “Joins the battle!” screen was definitely a victory worth celebrating.

There are also a handful of objectives to accomplish that will unlock even more Weapons, Passives, and more, and it was a pleasant surprise when five or more of them unlocked after one run. These types of games just know how to give you that dopamine rush that keeps you coming back for more.

This was only the demo, so we’ll see how the full game plays out, but after rescuing the two characters and getting most of the objectives after a couple of hours, I did feel a bit of tedium start to set in. My biggest problem with Vampire Survivors was always feeling that the start could be very, very slow, as you are so weak and doing the same things over and over again, and I felt this a few times during my hands-on.

items.title: A chat with Awesome Games Studio about Yet Another Zombie Survivors
items.summary: Awesome Games Studio recently did the big 1.0 release for Yet Another Zombie Survivors and it seems like quite an indie success - so here
items.content:
Awesome Games Studio recently did the big 1.0 release for Yet Another Zombie Survivors and it seems like quite an indie success - so here's a little chat.

I'm a big fan of these bullet heaven survivor-like games, after trying out probably hundreds of them at this point, with this being what I consider one of the best so this was a fun one.

Q: Could you introduce yourselves and how you go into game development?

"Hi, I'm Zbyszek! A fellow GamingOnLinux reader, and an industry unicorn. I've been dabbling in game development and other things related to video games since I can remember, going back to shoot'em'up game builder engines and editors on the Commodore 64. Professionally speaking, Awesome Games Studio is my first full-time job of this kind, and I've been here for 8 years already, enjoying the possibility I've been given of working on... well... awesome games! PS Thanks for the interview opportunity!"

Q: What exactly is Yet Another Zombie Survivors ("YAZS")? Why yet another?

"The tongue-in-cheek title of the game is actually part of a long-running series of games, previously composed of Yet Another Zombie Defense and its HD version/sequel. "YAZS" began its development as another title in the "Defense" series, but when we played Vampire Survivors when it was first getting popular, we loved it, and thought we could do our own spin on the formula. As such, the project switched to "Survivors" around 2023. I often say that the title is cheesy because we aren't afraid of it being a detracting point from the game. You could say it's a lesson we'd like to teach fellow gamers: what's important is the content of the package, not its label, and we're proud to have released one heck of a game!"

Q: The game released the big 1.0 back in August - how did it go?

"Awesome! Naturally, there was a lot of stress and there were time-critical tasks to cover around the release date. We're but a small team, and the expectations from our community were high. Looking back, we can safely say that the release was a great success. We might not have reached the online player peak on Steam that we've clocked when the Early Access version released, but nearly reaching 10,000 active players at a single moment in time can definitely be considered a great victory for an indie dev. For this, we're really thankful to our awesome players, also the ones that play the game on the console platforms and GOG. While it's already a full package, we're continuing our work on improving the game for everyone to enjoy it to its fullest."

Q: What do you think about discoverability issues developers face on stores like Steam? There's thousands of games releasing all the time.

"It's tragic. The number of indie games trying to break out into the light of day is staggering, and so many of those are great passion projects that often don't get their time to shine. Even that little title that helped shape what YAZS has become - Vampire Survivors - was for some time a totally unknown game until streamers decided to pick it up, likely at random. There are lots of similar stories of indie hits, which began as titles that no one knew about. Once again, it's incredibly tragic, and there's not much we can do about it, except support each other on social media and spread the word about the passion projects we discovered. Steam is full of incredible games, and we hope Valve will continue its work on making them more discoverable."

Q: Tell us a bit about your game development workflow, what are you using?

"We've been using the Unity engine for most of our projects for a long time now. It comes with the default set of tools that I believe most other devs use, from Visual Studio to Photoshop, so there won't be anything really groundbreaking here for me to cover. Still, we try to use interesting tools that we find out about. As an example, for our other upcoming title - HELLREAPER - we're doing the 2D animation part in Spine2D, which isn't really a popular tool, but it allows us to make the in-game art look like it's 3D, while it's not."

Q: How challenging was it to get the game Steam Deck Verified? Any annoyances?

"I'd like to do my best not to downplay the titanic job our main programmer did to get us accepted into it, but I believe it wasn't all THAT difficult. This is in big part due to the fact that we've had our previous titles accepted already (most after implementing a few tweaks), so we knew what was required by the platform holder to get the green checkmark. The hardest part was finding time to implement the changes required, while simultaneously doing our best to work on new content for the game. Thankfully, lots of the work was already done, as we're developing YAZS from the ground up as a very accessible game, with lots of customizable options and full controller support. Still, we needed to comply with random quirks like the minimum required font size that can be displayed on the screen at any given time, so it wasn't a cakewalk, really. Also, some of us have Steam Decks of our own, so it definitely helped a lot with understanding the ecosystem and the needs Deck users have."

items.title: New Action Roguelike PC Game is Essentially Minecraft Meets Vampire Survivors
Acclaimed Vampire Survivors-Inspired Survival Game Hits Switch Next Month
items.content:
If you're one of many people who got hopelessly addicted to Vampire Survivors , then you might want to keep an eye out for Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor , which launches on Switch on 9th October 2026 .

Developed by Funday Games, DRG: Survivor launched in early access on 14th February 2024 before receiving a full release on Windows and Xbox Series X|S on 17th September 2025. It's been well-received too, earning a score of 8/10 from IGN and 90% from PC Gamer , with the latter concluding its review with a line that will undoubtedly catch your attention:

"Vampire Survivors is no longer the king of the genre."

So yeah, sounds pretty good. But what's it all about? Well, as a spin-off of the 4-player co-op shooter Deep Rock Galactic , DRG: Survivor uses auto-shooting mechanics to fend off hordes of enemies, uncover valuable loot within the mines, and upgrade your characters with powerful new abilities.

It's chaotic, it's colourful, and it's very pretty, so we're really looking forward to checking this out on Switch.

items.title: Legacy of the Bloodmoon is out now!
items.summary: 🔴Legacy of the Bloodmoon Hi everyone! Our darkest expansion for Vampire Survivors is out now and at a special price: one money! (or as low as we could go, depending on regional currency). Yes, the finance team wants to kill me. https://sto
items.content:
🔴Legacy of the Bloodmoon

Hi everyone! Our darkest expansion for Vampire Survivors is out now and at a special price: one money! (or as low as we could go, depending on regional currency). Yes, the finance team wants to kill me. https://store.steampowered.com/app/4781330/Vampire_Survivors_Legacy_of_the_Bloodmoon/ This expansion pack follows Clan Bloodmoon as they retrace the pilgrimage of Saint Baal’Thasar, in search of a paradise lit by (you guessed it) a bright red moon. There is also an ancient manor that may or may not hide the secret of immortality. Legacy of the Bloodmoon contains:
  • 12 new villains friendly characters
  • 16+ new weapons and evolutions, including a FireBall
  • 11 savage new music tracks
  • 1 new adventure
  • 1 new very large stage

Other platforms

All platforms will be on stable version 1.16.100 or higher. Version 1.16.105, which contains performance improvements and a fix to an ability for Baal'Thasar, should arrive on Android and Nintendo Switch by the end of next week.

🔴Legacy of the Moonspell

But that's not all! Our very first expansion, Legacy of the Moonspell, is also getting extra content and, if you don't already own it, it is also at a special price: https://store.steampowered.com/app/2230760/Vampire_Survivors_Legacy_of_the_Moonspell/ - 5 extra weapons - 4 extra characters - 1 extra music track - buffs to the original cast of characters

🔴Version 1.16.100

The game has been updated to version 1.16.100 to handle the new content, but also to add performance and QOL improvements: - Banish: after banishing an item, you can keep using the LevelUp menu. - Quickstart: it now tries to pick a character and/or stage that is linked to a missing unlock - Special passives buff (Operation Guns, Emergency Meeting): they can now be found in ArmaDios and as a LevelUp option whenever they'd normally be available, and even if the player has reached the passive limit. - Reworked several main framework features to improve CPU and memory usage across the board - Fixed some Drowners not spawning - Fixed Gorgeous Moon and Big Fuzzy Fist missing sprites - Fixed some weapons glitching textures when paired with other weapons (eg. Fleuret) - Fixed damage numbers glitching at low FPS and improved their perfomance - Fixed stuttering when the stage minutes change - Fixed purchase of MAX Golden Eggs - Fixed Luck bonus glitching on Chula-Reh and Henry - Ongoing work to improve visibility of interactable objects/layers You can find the rest of the patchnotes since version 1.15.100 here: https://steamcommunity.com/app/1794680/discussions/0/583931105981294494/

🔴Platform achievements

We're trying once again to find a way to add achievements without affecting the completion rate for the main game, but we don't know if it will be possible. Regardless, new Steam achievements for the base game, Moonspell, and Bloodmoon will be added in patch 1.17, scheduled to release before the end of the year. Once the achievements are published, they'll unlock automatically if you have already obtained them in game, so nothing is lost.

🔴VS Soundtrack

The soundtrack will be updated in a few days with the missing tracks from the base game, Moonspell, and Bloodmoon! Legacy of the Bloodmoon ended up having 11 music tracks instead of 8, but by now I think we're all pretty used to content creep 🤷‍♂️ Please remember that due to the legal insanities of music licensing, we are not allowed to distribute tracks from Operation Guns, Ode to Castlevania, or Emerald Diorama. But we're still trying... Well, that's enough of the doom and gloom of Bloodmoon for me, need a nice sunny place to take a break 😎 Let's see what the options are: 🩻- darkest depths of Moongolow -> Vampire Crawlers 1.1 👻- Tokyo overrun by cursed spirits -> JJKRS 1.0 ☠️- -> top secret - NDA - 0.1 ⛱️- Biggus Diccus Theme Park -> Vampire Survivors 1.17 Looks like there's a clear winner! Thank you and see you in the next patch! ⛱️ - Luca

items.title: Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton
items.summary: Hi everyone, we have a lot happening around new games and Vampire Survivors, so here's a gigantic news post! 🟣- Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton 🔴- Vampire Survivors 1.15 🔴- Legacy of the Bloodmoon teasers 🔴- Legacy of the Moonspell in
items.content:
Hi everyone, we have a lot happening around new games and Vampire Survivors, so here's a gigantic news post! 🟣- Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton 🔴- Vampire Survivors 1.15 🔴- Legacy of the Bloodmoon teasers 🔴- Legacy of the Moonspell info 🔴- Workshop Support for Vampire Survivors 🔴- ARG and Character Community Challenge winners 🔴- Vampire Survivors Comics 🔵- Vampire Crawlers updates 🟢- PoncleUp

🟣 Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton

A few days back we announced Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton in collaboration with Shueisha Games! Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton is a game like Vampire Survivors, but with a twist: you'll be able to play an 8-player survivors royale PvPvE mode! Some in-game names and terminology are still in development and may be subject to change. While every player plays in their own world, you accumulate points by defeating curses and sorcerers, and with every 100 points accumulated you get to choose a Rule Change that can affect everyone's game. Some Rule Changes are INSANE, but for now we'll just reveal the simple ones you can see in the trailer (silence, slow, steal points...). But Rule Changes aren't the only way to interact with other players. Introducing a world first, mind blowing, unbelievable game mechanic: PRESS A BUTTON. While you move your auto-attacking character, your special attack also builds up. By PRESSING A BUTTON when the special attack is ready, you get to unleash your character's Special Attack, or, if that character can, a DOMAIN EXPANSION! Other players can be caught in the effect of your Domain or Special Attack, so you have to keep an eye on other players' position and special-bar status. A very important aspect of the 8-players mode is the Live Match Status Feed (working name). This big chunk of UI on the left side of the screen constantly updates in real time, acting not only as a scoreboard, but also sending out warnings and all kind of information about what the other players are up to. At the end of the 15 minutes battle royale, the 2 players with the most points will face one another in a 19 seconds duel. Despite the online focus, Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton is a game you can also play alone, in a mission-based mode, just like Vampire Survivors. If you don't ever want to go online, you'll still be able to play the 8-players battle royale mode against bots. This is a game you buy once and can play anytime. We'll keep supporting the game after launch, with our usual style of content updates. So forget about gatcha elements or a forever-evolving PvP meta keeping your time and wallet hostages: our focus here are fun and affordability. Apologies if you had enough of this wall of text, but I kepty mouth shut for almost two years and I haven't even got to the technical bits yet! Yes, the game runs on the Vampire Survivors - First Survivaton framework, so you can expect that same familiar experience playing it, but we had to do several unique tweaks for Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble Survivaton. Other than the obvious, completely new networking for the gameplay and Live Match Status Feed, we have doubled the resolution at which the game runs. That allowed us to completely rebuild the whole VFX pipeline so that we could re-create the distinctive look of Curse Energy and the changes the whole stage depending on activated Domain Expansions or Special Attacks. Another reason to double the resolution was to properly display the UI (that has been completely reworked at framework level) and the Live Match Status Feed, that is capable of also streaming gameplay snippets from other online players. You'll see a lot of other tweaks, like the fact that characters look different if they are seen from the left or from the right, a "default attack" per character that triggers without any weapon, or walls that are actually solid to name a few. Then there are other changes that won't be noticeable until you get to play the game. For example, while we are going by the same content-unlock-philosophy as Vampire Survivors, we are completely reworking the progression in the various game modes and also per-character, so that every game mode will feel fresh even to VS veterans. That's all for now, I hope you have enjoyed the trailer; my favourite part was that bit were Gojo takes a walk.

🔴 Vampire Survivors 1.15 available on all platforms

- Nintendo Switch 1 and 2 - Android - iOS & Apple Arcade - PS4 and PS5 - Xbox - EGS In the following weeks there will be small updates quite often on all platforms to bring them all on the same version, because all platforms have the same content, but not the same bugfixes and tweaks. Please join the Discord or keep an eye on the Updates version of the wiki if you're interested in knowing the fixes in each update (I won't spam Steam News every week for small tweaks).

🔴 New Moonspell Content spoilers

When we'll launch Legacy of the Bloodmoon, we'll also update the contents of Legacy of the Moonspell. It will get 7 new unlocks, that will deliver:

  • 4 new weapons: LunarMight, LunarSight, LunarBight, and LunarFlight [/*]
  • 1 Special Evolution: Argent Flow [/*]
  • 1 new passive Weapon: Pearl Magatama [/*]
  • 4 new characters [/*]
  • 1 new music track [/*]
  • some buffs to the original cast of characters: [/*]
- Menya Moonspell gets Overheal +16: activates her starting weapon. - Babi-Onna gets Overheal +16: gains a temporary bonus to MoveSpeed (that also means she attacks faster). - Megalo Menya Moonspell gets Overheal +16: activates her first weapon. - Megalo Syuuto Moonspell gets Overheal +16: equipped Blood weapons gain extra damage. - McCoy-Oni gets Overheal +16: gains a Reroll. - Gav'Et-Oni gets \.This will be a free update, in fact last month we have actually dropped the price of Legacy of the Moonspell to balance out a bit the cost/content ratio of the various expansions.

🔴 Bloodmoon character tease

Legacy of the Bloodmoon is almost complete and we will be able to start testing and submissions soon! That means we'll have an actual release date soon too. In the meantime, here's a Character Spotlight video about Malice Bloodmoon:

🔴 ARG and Community Character Competition winners

Congratulations to the trio of winners of the Lucca Comics ARG: Jenoss, Miryel, Siming, and GIU_LLS (:poemg:?), and to DissonantSynth for winning the Community Challenge! We're finally getting into the design stage of the characters, with a first implementation that will soon be shared with the winners, behind the scenes, to start iterating together on gameplay mechanics. You can expect a few surprises and little extras about them when they'll make their appearance in the game! Baron Husker and Sefi Rotto (:poemg:?) will come alive in a later update, v1.17

🔴 First steps for Steam Workshop support

Instead of waiting the conclusion of the current cycles of updates for Vampire Survivors as originally planned, we will develop modding support over time, one feature at a time. Feature 1 will be about adding CUSTOM (private/local) and WORKSHOP (public/Steam Workshop) characters! Please join the Discord or use the public-beta forum if you're interested in trying out custom characters before they go live on the main branch, in a future update (currently aiming for v1.17)

🔴 Vampire Survivors Comics

Vampire Survivor is getting comics! We've been working with Titan Comics on a 4-issue series, written by David Hazan and illustrated by Jimm Kucaj, with the first issue coming out this September, available in 3 cover variants. Some familiar Vampire Survivors will go through Mad Forest, Inlaid Library, Dairy Plant, and a few other places, and there might even be some lore in there. Issue #1 is available to pre-order from your local comic shop or from Forbidden Planet if you're in the UK / EU. You can find out more about the comics on the Titan Comics website.

🔵 Vampire Crawlers: first QOL update

Our first update to Vampire Crawlers add an Endless mode and several QOL improvements! You can find more details, the strategy behind future updates, and some content spoilers in the Steam News here.

🟢 Countup to the next announcement

Look, we're doing a lot of stuff across several small teams. I'm always happy to write the Steam News but I cannot bombard your feed with everything we're doing. Also took me something like 3 weeks to set this all up. So if you'd like to hear about what we're doing a bit more often, then please visit poncleup.com to see a recap or subscribe to our newsletter. It's a countup instead of a countdown because, as you might have noticed, we're release-date-averse and have no idea ourselves when we'll drop something new 🤷‍♂️ Just know that the newsletters are written by the marketing team :vsskull: Alright, I'm done with work, time to go back having fun on my secret project. Thank you everyone, I'll leave you in the self-proclaimed capable hands of the marketing team! - Luca

items.title: Vampire Survivors: Legacy of the Bloodmoon is coming this summer!
items.summary: Hi everyone! As anticipated several months ago, we’ve been working on several core systems of VS to be able to keep making more content, increase stability, and improve performance. It’s been a while so we have quite a few things to cover t
items.content:
Hi everyone! As anticipated several months ago, we’ve been working on several core systems of VS to be able to keep making more content, increase stability, and improve performance. It’s been a while so we have quite a few things to cover today: - a new expansion for VS - a new update - a new poncle team in Japan - the very sensible reason why Vampire Survivors has a sub-title now 🤷‍♂️

Vampire Survivors Update 1.15 (The Wet One) is out now on Steam!

You can find all details about 1.15 below, now here’s a stupid summer trailer about it:

Major QOL improvements

  • Multiple Save Slots (about time!)
  • Character Setup panel for skins, egg selection, etc…
  • Content filters in Character Selection and Unlocks menu
  • Stability improvements for late game and low-end platforms
  • Reduced loading times (more noticeable on other platforms than PC)

New content

  • 1 New Stage: The Lycaeum
  • 2 New Characters
  • either 2 or 10 new weapons 🤷‍♂️
  • 3 New Darkanas
  • 1 New Music Track
  • 3 new Relics, of which 1 Secret rather than Unlockable

Other tweaks and features

  • "Random LevelUp" can now be toggled during a run if it is already unlocked on the Stage menu
  • Added option to Unbanish a weapon when picking it up from the stage
  • Buffed a few weapons like Magi-Stone and Mille Bolle Blu
  • Rendering fixes for a few weapons, including birds, Prismatic Missile, Runetracer…
Patch 1.15 will be released on all other platforms a bit later, by the end of the month, due to platform-specific optimizations and differences in save slots management. On the bright side, we will also be releasing a Nintendo Switch 2 version, with better performance and mouse support!

Vampire Survivors: Legacy of the Bloodmoon is coming Summer 2026

https://store.steampowered.com/app/4781330/Vampire_Survivors_Legacy_of_the_Bloodmoon/ Vampire Survivors: Legacy of the Bloodmoon is our “accidental” next expansion and the evil twin to Legacy of the Moonspell. The original plan was just to make a little content update to Legacy of the Moonspell. Since it’s the first and smallest VS expansion, it felt right to try to balance its value a little. Needless to say, ideas started to flow and everything spiraled into a much bigger project. I’m not sure I’ll ever learn at this stage. In the end, Legacy of the Moonspell will be getting its content buff (7 new unlocks) and Legacy of the Bloodmoon will live a life of its own. This expansion pack follows Clan Bloodmoon as they retrace the pilgrimage of Saint Baal’Thasar, in search of a paradise lit by (you guessed it) a bright red moon. There is also an ancient manor that may or may not hide the secret of immortality. Legacy of the Bloodmoon will contain:
  • 12 new villains friendly characters
  • 16+ new weapons and evolutions, including a FireBall
  • 8 savage new music tracks
  • 1 new adventure
  • 1 new very large stage
  • Interesting bits and bobs I won’t spoil at this time
But there’s more. Legacy of the Bloodmoon will cost approximately 1 money (0.99 USD), and Legacy of the Moonspell will receive a price cut and also be priced 1 money :) You can find all details about Legacy of the Bloodmoon below, now here’s a villainous trailer about it:

Vampire Survivors - First Survivaton

Among the many projects we’re working on (approximately 15 projects, not 15 games, please don’t panic) there is also a lineup of Survivaton games. It’s definitely a meaningful word that means “survive a ton” and nothing else. These are games like Vampire Survivors, developed internally at poncle, tied to IPs that might need unique game mechanics, a different graphic style, or are so expansive that ultimately deserve their own standalone game (compared to making a DLC for VS). I’d love to make examples, but I’d have to spoil way too much. Being developed internally, we’ll be able to guarantee affordability and worthwhile titles. Since a good 90% of global VS players aren’t reached by the Steam news (or are not interested in gaming news in general), the best way to also let them know that the Survivatons are tied directly to VS is to also call VS a Survivaton, hence the new sub-title. Please note there’s a dash before First Survivaton instead of a semi-colon, because DLCs exist... The next time I name a game I’ll remember to not use something as generic as “Monster Hunter” as inspiration please know I love Monster Hunter 💌

poncle Japan

We can finally say we are building poncle Japan! It will be poncle, but in Japan. The new studio is headed by Sawaki Takeyasu, known for his work on Devil May Cry, Ōkami, and El Shaddai: Ascension of the Metatron. Having a studio in Japan will simplify and speed up the work we do with all our Japanese partners, and also bring new opportunities for collabs. It’s too soon to say what the team will be working on; we are planning to fully open the studio by the end of 2026. Now it's time for all the FAQs and info blocks, thanks for reading and waiting patiently for this update! - Luca

Legacy of the Bloodmoon FAQs

When does it release? Summer 2026. What do you define as summer? Not winter. How much does it cost? Around £0.95, with regional pricing varying by platform and country. Why will Legacy of the Moonspell’s price change too? It felt right to adjust the price so that it’s more balanced compared to the amount of content of the other expansions. Please note that some stores have minimum prices in certain countries. In some places, Moonspell was already too cheap to make it cheaper. What about Tides of the Foscari then? Please at least wait for Moonspell and Bloodmoon before asking for more, we know we know 😭 Will Moonspell get new content too? Yes, 7 new unlocks for a few more weapons and characters. Is Vampire Survivors still getting free updates? Yes of course, there’s still plenty on the roadmap.

Update 1.15 Full spoilers

♫ Murder on the Seafloor Composed and arranged by Filippo Vicarelli.

Quick content guide:

  • Collect a total of 50 Vacuums to unlock The Lycaeum stage
  • Find the Penshin Fatcha in The Lycaeum and see all its evolutions to unlock it permanently
  • Survive 20 minutes in The Lycaeum to unlock Para Kooleo
  • Trigger a Lavatrix Machina with Para Kooleo to unlock Darkana VIII - Edge of the Earth
  • Buy the Survarocchi at the top of The Lycaeum to unlock them for any character
  • Buy the Green Eyes Vizard at the top of The Lycaeum to be able to find Bat Dragons in other stages
  • Defeat any Bat Dragon (Currently available in Mad Forest and Il Molise) to unlock the Unearthly Bolt wea;on
  • Evolve the Unearthly Bolt with a maxed Tirajisú to unlock Big Troubler
  • Defeat any Bat Dragon with Big Troubler and Arcana 0 - Game Killer to unlock Darkana 0 - Stake to your Heart
  • Survive 15 minutes in Inverse Boss Rash with Random Events and Random Level Ups to unlock Darkana XIX - Heir of Fate
  • Defeat 2 unique Bat Dragons to unlock a new set of Survarots to purchase from Big Troubler

Detailed info

New stage: The Lycaeum An underwater-themed stage where you press some buttons, beat some crabs, run to the center, kill more things, press more buttons, don’t die. The Drowner can only be defeated via raw damage or by reaching the top of the stage. Hidden treasures can be collected only using Mad Groove or Lavatrix Machina. Teleporters become active after reaching the top once. New character: Para Kooleo Starts with a Move Speed and Duration bonus. When his HP drops below a certain threshold it triggers a Vacuum. He also likes to evolve weapons. He has an abundance of skins. New character: Big Troubler Loves gold and gets trigger happy when he gets gold. The gold also loves him and will protect him at all costs. New weapon: Penshin Fatcha & Tonno Subito / Tonnado / Tonn’omoto / Tonn’oddeeo / Tonne / Unsurpassed / Miracle of Multiplication. Starting weapon for Para Kooleo. Select one of six tuna forms. Evolve it from one to another, stacking stats as you go. Evolve at least once to transform all the Vacuums pickup into "Lavatrix Machina". Then, if you choose to, evolve into the secret evolution, Miracle of Multiplication where everything happens at once. Does not require any items to evolve, but many, many treasure chests. New weapon: Unearthly Bolt & Spirit Disturbance Starting weapon of Big Troubler. Spawns green bolts that attack the closest enemy. It deals increasingly high damage if it Crits in rapid succession. The cap for this damage bonus is determined by Revivals. Evolve with a maxed out Tirajisú. The evolution spawns a green dragon that always deals critical hits. New relic: Green Eyes Vizard Bat Dragons will appear on the Stage Selection menu until they have been defeated at least once. They will appear on the map during a run, and they have to be activated by getting hit. Once active, time stops and enemy waves are changed until they are killed. You can fight them again in new runs, they simply won't be signaled in Stage Selection anymore after getting killed once. New Darkanas: 0 - Stake to your Heart Unlocked by defeating a Bat Dragon with Big Troubler while using the Game Killer Arcana. You will no longer be able to level up using experience gems. Instead, when defeating an enemy, they will also drop a Gold Coin, that you’ll be able to spend at a special merchant to buy weapons. Gold coins will also become your health: don't reach 0 (and quit before Red Death deals the usual 65535 damage per hit to you) New Darkanas: VIII - Edge of the Earth Unlocked by triggering a Lavatrix Machina with Para Kooleo. Gain Thorns and Move Speed locked at 200%, ignore walls, destroy light sources upon contact, and attract things that normally aren’t attracted by a Magnet, like treasure chests. New Darkanas: XIX - Heir of Fate Unlocked by surviving 15 minutes in inverse Boss Rash with Random Events and Random Level Ups enabled. While active, defeating enemies with Fire damage causes them to drop Scorched Souls. Additionally, a Nduja Fritta Tanto will trigger when the character's Health dips to a certain point. New Relics: Survarocchi Unlocked by purchasing it from the Big Troubler merchant in The Lycaeum. Allows Survarot cards to spawn from light sources. Previously available only via the Ante Chamber dlc and a secret character, Survarots Enemahs (Secret rather than Unlockable) Unlocked by purchasing it from the Big Troubler merchant in The Lycaeum after defeating any two unique Bat Dragons. Adds an extra 18 cards based on various enemies to drafts of Survarot. For the full list of bugfixes, please see here: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1794680/view/693137145499484509

1.15 FAQs

How much is 1.15? It’s a free update. Can I now share DLCs when playing online? Not yet, in this patch we managed to do the groundwork to allow for DLC sharing, but we still have to complete the feature. Can I now use Cross-save on PS and Apple+? Not yet. We still don’t have the right policies in place to do that. What platforms is update 1.15 available on? Update 1.15 is launching on Steam first. Other platforms are planned to follow by the end of the month, including Xbox, PlayStation 4/5, Nintendo Switch, Android, iOS, and Epic Games Store. Is update 1.15 coming to Nintendo Switch 2? Yes! Update 1.15 will bring Vampire Survivors to Nintendo Switch 2 for the first time. It won’t arrive at the exact same time as the other platforms, but the current plan is for Nintendo Switch 2 support to follow around two weeks after update 1.15 (but don’t hold us to that). Where are the new achievements? We will sort out the new Steam achievements in the next patch (they will pop automatically). Hey are you still updating Vampire Crawlers? Yes of course, it’s taking longer than expected to release the first QOL improvements patch and a cute looking roadmap because we got stuck for days trying to exit the game.

items.title: Vampire Crawlers is out now!
items.summary: Today, we are releasing Vampire Crawlers, a new spin-off set in the Vampire Survivors universe. It takes the familiar chaos of Vampire Survivors and turns it into a casual, turn-based, card-driven BLOBBER with roguelite elements. We’ve talk
items.content:
Today, we are releasing Vampire Crawlers, a new spin-off set in the Vampire Survivors universe.

It takes the familiar chaos of Vampire Survivors and turns it into a casual, turn-based, card-driven BLOBBER with roguelite elements.

We’ve talked before about wanting to take some of the accidental core pillars of Vampire Survivors and apply them to other genres: accessibility, immediacy, affordability, replayability, lightheartedness, and the usual amount of flashy nonsense. Vampire Crawlers is the first attempt at that. 

Crawl through dungeons, build busted decks, master the TurboTurn™, and try to keep the run going long enough to pretend it was all planned. You can watch the launch trailer below.

(In other news, God appears briefly and remains unhelpful.)

Vampire Crawlers

The full game includes everything from the demo, plus more content, more fixes, and more improvements across the board. The game is built around:

  • TurboTurn™ combat: Turn-based combat without the wait. Queue your moves instantly and let the game resolve them at full speed.

    [/*]

  • The Combo: cards are played in ascending mana order, and each step multiplies the next card’s effect

    [/*]

  • Wild cards that let you extend the stack and push combos further

    [/*]

  • Deckbuilding through progression: level up to gain new cards, find power-ups, chase evolutions, and customize your runs

    [/*]

  • Character cards and summoned survivors that add more effects and help create larger cascades

    [/*]

  • Dungeon exploration with treasures, floor progression, and interactive points of interest

    [/*]

  • A pace you choose yourself: take your time and be tactical, or play turns as fast as you humanly can

    [/*]

The full version also launches with the fixes and improvements made after the demo feedback period, and we are planning to keep the demo available as well.

So all of us at poncle and Nosebleed Interactive would like to say thank you to everyone who played the demo, reported bugs, shared feedback, and generally tried to break things. That was genuinely useful.

Releasing now — $9.99 / €9.99 / £9.99

You can get Vampire Crawlers on Steam by clicking the link below.

Vampire Crawlers Original Soundtrack

Also releasing into the wild: the Vampire Crawlers Original Soundtrack.

The OST includes the game’s main theme, “Il Cuor non si Spaura,” composed by Yoko Shimomura, alongside tracks by Daniele Zandara, Filippo Vicarelli, and Michael Coviello. For a total of 32 tracks and over 1 hour of music for crawling purposes, available in MP3 and FLAC on Steam. It includes both the Crawling and Turbo versions, hidden tracks that are no longer hidden, and yes, there is a disco version of the inn theme.

You can listen here:

Or download here

FAQs

  • What platforms is the game on? Vampire Crawlers is available on Steam, Nintendo Switch, Xbox, and PlayStation. Mobile versions are planned for later in 2026.

    [/*]

  • How much does it cost? £9.99 / $9.99 / €9.99 / ¥1200.

    [/*]

  • How long to beat the game? Around 20 to 30 hours, and a bit longer if you are going for every unlock.

    [/*]

  • Does the game support controllers? Yes. Controller support is included.

    [/*]

  • Does the game support cross-save between different platforms? Not right now, but we’re looking into it in time for the mobile ports.

    [/*]

  • Will save data carry over on Steam if I played the demo? Yes. Demo progress can carry over to the full game on Steam.

    [/*]

More FAQ details here: Vampire Crawlers FAQ —

https://poncle.games/vampire-crawlers-faq

See you in the next news post. Happy crawling!

-From everyone at poncle and Nosebleed Interactive
